Policy on shift swaps
This section sets out how the desk handles it

Purpose: keep Companion Animal Travel Desk coverage steady, protect traveler service, and prevent gaps in care when staff must exchange duties. All shift swaps require prompt notice to the senior coordinator and a clear handoff of pending cases, especially where a live animal, a crate issue, or a border check is in progress. The staff member who gives away a shift remains responsible until the swap is approved and the receiving staff member has confirmed readiness.

A swap may proceed only when both staff members are qualified for the duties involved, both understand the current queue, and the desk can maintain service without delay. Species, temperament, and comfort notes must be reviewed before any transfer, and any special care plan must stay attached to the file. Do not leave a handoff incomplete. If a traveler is waiting at the counter or on the line, the outgoing staff member must stay available until the case is settled or reassigned.

When a claim, kennel, or lounge issue is active, the swap must be flagged at once so the next handler sees the full record. <<FACT F118>> The same applies to quarantine matters and reception planning. <<FACT F028>> Use calm, direct language in the log, and record any concern about the animal's safety, carrier condition, or traveler instructions before leaving the desk. <<FACT F021>>

Approval may be withheld if the change would weaken response coverage, interfere with live support, or cause confusion over ownership of an open case. Repeated late notices or informal handoffs are not acceptable. The desk lead may refuse any swap that leaves the service short or puts care standards at risk, and that decision is final for the shift in question.

Contact the senior coordinator at once for urgent approval, dispute handling, or any handoff that cannot be completed cleanly.
